use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

evidence_cards.content: Track reporting criteria are based on the requirements for the exchange of surveillance information and data usable in providing threat warning information among systems involved in joint operations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence defines the high-level objective (goal) of the track reporting process, which is to provide threat warning information through the exchange of surveillance data.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have correlated local sensor data to assume R2 of an IU.

source_locations.location: paragraph starting 'A C2 JU shall assume R2...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory state (correlated local sensor data) that must exist before the reporting logic for inactive/limited status units can be triggered.

evidence_cards.content: The system requires specific input conditions regarding J2 PPLI messages (e.g., not received for 40-60 seconds, NPS set to Inactive, or Drop Track message received) to transition to reporting an IU as a track.

source_locations.location: list items a through d under section 4.4.2.2.2

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific situational states (missing data, inactive status flags, drop commands) that constitute the preconditions for initiating the surveillance track report for these specific unit types.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a mandatory system capability (automatic correlation) that must exist before the C2 JU can effectively publish tracks to prevent dual designations, serving as a technical precondition for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: Each C2 JU which has a capability to originate and report real-time air, surface (maritime), land (ground), or space tracks shall have a capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the actor must possess the specific capability to perform common tracking prior to engaging in the reporting of these tracks.

evidence_cards.content: R² procedures for Air, Surface (Maritime), and Land (Ground) tracks are designed to ensure that only the JU having the best positional data available is reporting the track on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a system-level precondition: before any JU can publish a track, it must be determined via R² rules whether this JU has the best positional data — implying that R² evaluation is a prerequisite condition for publication eligibility.

evidence_cards.content: The first JU to report the track has R² on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an initial state precondition: if no other JU has reported the track yet, the current JU may assume reporting responsibility by default — meaning absence of prior reporters is a valid pre-condition for initiating publication.

evidence_cards.content: A JU transmits a track report for an Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track only when it has R² for that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Explicitly states a mandatory precondition: possession of R² (reporting responsibility) is required before transmission can occur — directly constraining when the use case can begin.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU capable of assuming R² for air, surface, or land tracks shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory system state (completion of checks and registration) that must hold before the C2 JU can begin publishing tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific time-based precondition (minimum delay) required before the use case can proceed to transmission.

evidence_cards.content: Automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific event (receipt of J2/J3 message) that triggers automatic processing actions within the C2 JU’s track management workflow, which is part of the broader use case of publishing surveillance tracks — specifically, it initiates decorrelation testing prior to publication decisions.

evidence_cards.content: A JU transmits a track report for an Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track only when it has R² for that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This rule defines the condition under which the C2 JU initiates the transmission of a track report, serving as the operational trigger for publishing surveillance tracks once reporting responsibility is established.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU initiates the publication of air and surface surveillance tracks after initially achieving Active status or returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific state transitions (achieving or returning to Active status) that serve as the entry point for the track reporting process described in this section.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for publishing track information occurs when a JU changes the Environment/Category of a track (specifically from Space to air; Air to space/surface/land; Surface to air/subsurface; Subsurface to surface; Land to air/surface; or Unknown to any category) or when a difference report regarding these categories is rejected by an operator action.

source_locations.location: Paragraph starting 'When a JU changes the Environment/Category...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This text defines the specific events (category change or rejection of difference report) that initiate the reporting/publishing process described in this section.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU reports the position of the track extrapolated to the time of transmission for real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific data transformation required during the publication of real-time tracks in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: Nonreal-time data shall be identified as such and time tags shall be provided; nonreal-time track positions shall not be extrapolated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the handling rules for non-real-time data within the publication process.

evidence_cards.content: Common tracking is defined as sharing of a common track number and shifting R² between C² JUs, where each tracked object normally will be reported by one C² JU while others withhold their reports to prevent cluttering the tactical plot.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the coordination mechanism (withholding reports) that occurs when multiple actors have track data, which is part of the normal interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These restrictions define constraints on automatic correlation that must be evaluated during the main flow of publishing surveillance tracks, as correlation is a prerequisite for determining reporting responsibility and track eligibility for publication.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction based on ID difference or different Mode II codes, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C2 IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies configurable exceptions to the default correlation restrictions, which may affect whether tracks are correlated (and thus eligible for publication) in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The velocity of Air, Surface (Maritime), and Land (Ground) tracks shall be reported as course and speed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory reporting format for track velocity data during publication.

evidence_cards.content: The speed shall be reported in data miles per hour of ground speed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the unit and type of speed required for the published track data.

evidence_cards.content: The course shall be reported in degrees with respect to true north.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the reference frame and unit for the course component of the published track data.

evidence_cards.content: Track identity as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1 is exchanged.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that track identity information is included in the exchange/publication process.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message to terminate reporting a track for which it currently has R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific system action that constitutes the publication/termination interaction sequence in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the time-based logic within the interaction sequence where the actor assumes responsibility and prepares to publish tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The system shall not transmit air or surface tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a mandatory procedural step in the main flow for publishing tracks: performing checks before transmission.

evidence_cards.content: The minimum wait time before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a specific temporal constraint (delay) within the interaction sequence of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action (either automatically or manually) to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary actor's responsibility and initiation step in the main flow when a specific condition (dual designation eligibility) is met during track reporting.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the concrete system interaction/action the actor performs to propagate the resolution decision to other units.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the specific data content included in the main flow message transmission.

evidence_cards.content: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the C² JU shall decorrelate the PPLI and local track data, then initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, reporting both the PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field as 'No Statement'.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where decorrelation triggers a new track report instead of maintaining correlation — diverging from main flow step 3 (correlation restrictions) and step 5 (common tracking), resulting in a valid published track under altered identity assumptions.

evidence_cards.content: When a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or when a non-J2.0 PPLI arrives with NPS set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or when a J7.0 Drop Track message is received, or when Geodetic Position Quality is set to 0, the C² JU assumes R² of the IU and reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG with Identity reported as Friend, Track Number/Platform/Activity values from prior messages, and PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator set to value 1.

source_locations.location: section 4.4.2.2.2 and its subpoints a–d and following paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines multiple alternative flows triggered by specific inactive/limited status conditions that cause the C² JU to assume reporting responsibility and publish a track — diverging from main flow step 4 (R² assumption after ~40s no remote report) by applying different thresholds or triggers (e.g., explicit drop track, quality=0, radio silence) while still achieving successful publication.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs that have the capability to automatically initiate tracks for release to the interface without operator action shall also have the capability to deactivate this automatic capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a valid alternative flow where the actor (C2 JU) disables the default automatic track initiation behavior, diverging from the standard automatic reporting process.

evidence_cards.content: Nonreal-time data shall be identified as such and time tags shall be provided. Nonreal-time track positions shall not be extrapolated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative path for publishing non-real-time tracks, which differs from the main flow requirement of extrapolating real-time track positions to the time of transmission.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1. Systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These restrictions define alternative paths where automatic correlation is inhibited during the correlation step of the main flow, representing legal divergences from the canonical success scenario that still allow for manual correlation or other resolution methods without failing the overall use case.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² on a common track if its local TQ at the time of transmission exceeds the received TQ by 2 or more.

first image, paragraph under 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item c

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative condition for assuming reporting responsibility (R²) based on quality thresholds, diverging from the standard first-reporter rule.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has local real-time data and nonreal-time data were received.

source_locations.location: first image, paragraph under 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item d
first image, paragraph under 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item d

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative path where possession of superior local real-time data allows a JU to assume reporting responsibility over existing non-real-time reports.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.

source_locations.location: second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item e
second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item e

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow triggered by timeout thresholds, allowing a JU to take over reporting responsibility when remote updates cease.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

source_locations.location: second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item f
second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item f

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow triggered by a specific 'Drop Track' message, allowing a JU to reclaim reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0 shall assume R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.

source_locations.location: second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item g
second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item g

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow for low-quality (TQ=0) tracks where local updates trigger assumption of reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J2 PPLI message (with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure) from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

source_locations.location: second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item h
second image, paragraph continuing 'REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY', item h

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow triggered by status indicators (Inactive/Radio Silence/Failure) in PPLI messages, allowing a receiving JU to assume reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU may override the minimum wait time (12 seconds for air/surface tracks) in cases where operational necessity requires a shorter wait time or none at all.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a valid alternative path to the main flow's mandatory wait step, allowing immediate transmission under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU may perform the reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration as either an automatic or manual function.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a variant in how the pre-transmission checks are executed within the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field in the J7.2 message is set to value 0, it indicates that a reverse correlation request would be acceptable; when set to value 1, it indicates such a request would be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative path during dual designation resolution where the receiving IU may accept or reject a reverse correlation based on the RV field value — diverging from the main flow’s automatic/manual initiation by the originating JU.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine whether to originate a reverse correlation request or reject the original correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies how receiving IUs can initiate an alternative successful path (reverse correlation) instead of accepting the original correlation — a legal divergence from the main flow step of transmitting J7.2 with retained/dropped TNs.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection (see paragraph 4.7.3.2.c).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines another variant of the main flow: manual initiation of correlation with conditional acceptance — representing a still-successful alternative path that diverges from automatic initiation.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU receives or generates a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection), it shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow where correlation is rejected but the system continues operation under a time-based restriction rather than terminating — a legal variant path that diverges from the main correlation acceptance flow.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative successful path: instead of automatic correlation, the system triggers human intervention via alerting, allowing resolution through voice coordination — still achieving the goal without automation.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of three restrictions applies: (1) tracks are of different E/C or have existing E/C conflict; (2) one track is simulated and the other live; (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow where automatic acceptance occurs by default (RV=3), but only if no exclusionary conditions apply — representing a conditional success path distinct from the standard correlation initiation in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs that have the capability to automatically initiate tracks for release to the interface without operator action shall also have the capability to deactivate this automatic capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an exception handling path: when a C2 JU has automatic track initiation enabled but needs to suppress it (e.g., due to operational constraints or error conditions), it must be able to deactivate the automation — representing a controlled exit from an otherwise automated flow.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1. Systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines explicit exception conditions under which automatic correlation is prohibited during track publishing, constituting error or restriction handling paths that diverge from normal correlation flow.

evidence_cards.content: The restrictions on automatic correlation do not apply to manual correlation. No other correlation restrictions shall be applied for two tracks which pass the correlation tests specified in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies scope of exception flow — manual correlation bypasses these restrictions, establishing an alternative path when automatic correlation is blocked.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction for ID conflicts or differing Mode II codes. Use of this capability will be subject to interface coordination and must be promulgated to all C² IUs. If the use changes, all participating C² IUs will be informed through voice communication or other communications media. In lieu of specific interface direction, all IUs will restrict automatic correlation by default.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes configurable override mechanism for exception conditions, including procedural requirements for coordination and notification — part of exception handling workflow.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition where reporting responsibility is lost due to superior remote data quality, interrupting the normal publication flow.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track upon reception of a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition where reporting responsibility is lost due to tie-breaking by station number when track quality is equal, interrupting the normal publication flow.

evidence_cards.content: In the event of a conflict between locally derived information and information reported on the interface, the C2 JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific exception handling path for data conflicts during track reporting, detailing the allowed resolution mechanisms (message, procedure, or voice).

evidence_cards.content: When a JU receives a Surveillance message or a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message in which the air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) Environment/Category and ID are different from the local Environment/Category and ID, the Environment/Category conflict shall be processed and resolved prior to the resolution of the ID conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory processing order for resolving conflicting surveillance data, constituting an exception flow where standard reporting is interrupted by conflict resolution logic.

evidence_cards.content: If an Environment/Category conflict is detected, no further processing to detect an ID conflict need occur.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exit path for the ID conflict detection sub-process when a higher-priority Environment/Category conflict exists.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU receives a Surveillance message in which the Exercise Indicator is different from local Exercise Indicator data or a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message in which the Exercise Indicator is different from the local Exercise Indicator, a conflict exists and the operator shall be alerted for manual resolution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific exception condition (Exercise Indicator mismatch) that triggers an alert and requires manual intervention, deviating from automatic processing.

evidence_cards.content: Exercise Indicator conflicts will be resolved prior to ID or Identity Amplifying Descriptor Conflict resolution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the priority hierarchy for resolving multiple simultaneous conflicts during the exception handling process.

evidence_cards.content: Identity Amplifying Descriptor conflicts are processed in the same manner as ID conflicts.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies the handling procedure for a specific type of identity data conflict within the exception flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the locally held Environment/Category of a track is different from the Environment/Category received in a J3.X or a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message for that track, the operator shall be alerted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the trigger condition for an operator alert when local and remote environment data disagree, initiating an exception handling path.

evidence_cards.content: This alert shall be provided even in those cases where the received Environment/Category is not implemented.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a boundary condition for the alerting mechanism, ensuring exceptions are flagged even if the incoming data format is unsupported.

evidence_cards.content: If the local data and the received data differ as to whether the TN is assigned to a point or to a track, the operator shall be alerted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific data structure conflict (Point vs Track assignment) that triggers an exception alert requiring operator attention.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 2) message, it shall reject any received data on that track that differs for a 30-second lock-out period, except for ID data from the controlling unit of the track and for processing an Exercise Status Order.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception flow behavior when a transmission occurs: the system enters a lock-out state rejecting differing data, with specific exceptions to this rejection rule.

evidence_cards.content: After reception of the J7.0 (ACT = 2) message, JUs shall accept different data prior to the completion of the 30-second lockout period provided the different data is from the same source that originated the previous J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception path where the standard lock-out restriction is overridden if the new data comes from the original source.

evidence_cards.content: After reception of the J7.0 (ACT = 2) message, JUs shall accept different ID data prior to the completion of the 30-second lockout period provided the different ID data is from the controlling unit.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a second exception path where the lock-out restriction is overridden for ID data coming specifically from the controlling unit.

evidence_cards.content: Units receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 2) Change Data Order message containing an ID of Pending shall not accept that order.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an error handling path where a specific invalid condition (ID of Pending) causes the receiving unit to reject the order.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving JUs which do not implement the changed Environment/Category and have R² on the track must cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow triggered by a capability mismatch (lack of implementation), resulting in the termination of reporting and transmission of a drop track message.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU (as a receiving IU) receives a J7.2 Correlation message requesting correlation of two tracks, it shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the condition under which the main flow step of resolving dual designation (Step 6) results in an exception where the receiving unit rejects the request.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the receiving IU transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exit path and specific error code (RV=2) for the exception flow when a correlation request is rejected by the receiving IU.

evidence_cards.content: The originating JU indicates in the J7.2 message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation; when the RV field is set to value 1, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a constraint-based exception condition where a receiving IU cannot successfully execute a reverse correlation variant because the originator explicitly prohibits it.

evidence_cards.content: After successful publication of air and surface surveillance tracks, the track data is available for exchange with systems involved in joint operations, ensuring that: (a) the information on the track is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible; (b) data are correlated and dual designation is minimized; and (c) the proper rules for reporting a track are followed.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the observable system state after successful track publication — specifically, that published tracks meet criteria enabling their use in joint operations for threat warning, which constitutes the postcondition of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: For real-time tracks, the position reported is extrapolated to the time of transmission; for nonreal-time tracks, positions are not extrapolated and are identified with time tags.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.4.2 TRACK REPORTING, item c and d

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the final form of the published track data — a concrete attribute of the system state after successful publication — distinguishing how real-time vs. nonreal-time track positions are handled in the output.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU retains reporting responsibility (R²) on a track until it is relinquished in accordance with the R² rules or until the track is dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state regarding reporting responsibility persistence after successful track publication, which constitutes an immediate observable postcondition of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The air and surface surveillance tracks have been transmitted to the interface with identity, position (extrapolated for real-time or time-tagged for non-real-time), course in degrees true north, and speed in data miles per hour ground speed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific state of the system after the track publication action is successfully completed.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU has resolved all conflicts between locally derived information and interface-reported information for the published tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that a key state of data consistency is achieved as part of the successful reporting process.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU has assumed Reporting Responsibility (R²) for any uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks being reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that the system has formally taken ownership of the tracks it publishes, a necessary post-condition for valid track exchange.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message identifying the track number (TN) to be retained and the TN to be dropped to resolve dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific state change regarding track numbers resulting from the successful resolution of dual designations during the publication process.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the successful postcondition that the correlation request is accepted by other system units in the absence of specific rejection criteria.
